changeSet.comment: holding_status marks a position as still held or fully exited; result_type separates a plain withdrawal from the transfer leg introduced by issue #205, which reuses this table rather than adding its own (issue #204).
changeSet.sql: CREATE TYPE finances.holding_status AS ENUM ('ACTIVE', 'COMPLETED'); CREATE TYPE finances.result_type AS ENUM ('WITHDRAWAL', 'TRANSFER');

rollback.sql: DROP TYPE finances.result_type; DROP TYPE finances.holding_status;

changeSet.author: ${claude}
changeSet.comment: Every existing holding is still held, so ACTIVE is the correct backfill

changeSet.author: ${claude}
changeSet.comment: One row per exit from any of the three holding kinds. net_amount and profit are generated rather than written, so no caller can store a total that disagrees with its own parts. quantity is null for funds, which have no quantity to exit.
changeSet.sql: CREATE TABLE finances.results ( id BIGINT GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY PRIMARY KEY, external_id UUID NOT NULL DEFAULT gen_random_uuid() UNIQUE, stock_holding_id BIGINT NULL REFERENCES finances.stock_holdings(id) ON DELETE CASCADE, crypto_holding_id BIGINT NULL REFERENCES finances.crypto_holdings(id) ON DELETE CASCADE, fund_holding_id BIGINT NULL REFERENCES finances.fund_holdings(id) ON DELETE CASCADE, result_type finances.result_type NOT NULL, result_date DATE NOT NULL, quantity NUMERIC NULL CHECK (quantity > 0), gross_amount NUMERIC NOT NULL CHECK (gross_amount >= 0), fees NUMERIC NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 CHECK (fees >= 0), taxes NUMERIC NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 CHECK (taxes >= 0), cost_basis NUMERIC NOT NULL CHECK (cost_basis >= 0), net_amount NUMERIC GENERATED ALWAYS AS (gross_amount - fees - taxes) STORED, profit NUMERIC GENERATED ALWAYS AS (gross_amount - fees - taxes - cost_basis) STORED, created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(), CONSTRAINT results_exactly_one_holding CHECK ( (stock_holding_id IS NOT NULL)::INT + (crypto_holding_id IS NOT NULL)::INT + (fund_holding_id IS NOT NULL)::INT = 1 ) );

changeSet.author: ${claude}
${claude}
changeSet.comment:
Rebuild both views so they report net of what has been withdrawn. Both are dropped and recreated rather than replaced: holdings_report_rows is defined FROM holdings_overview, and Postgres refuses to change a view's column list while a dependent view exists.
The withdrawn totals are read through scalar correlated subqueries, not a join. A join to finances.results would multiply the existing SUM over lots by the number of result rows, silently inflating quantity and cost_basis on any holding exited more than once.
Only stock and crypto subtract the withdrawn quantity from current_value, because there it is derived from quantity. A fund withdrawal decrements fund_holdings.current_value directly, so subtracting again would double-count; only its cost_basis is netted here.
Asymmetry worth noting: holdings_overview exposes status so consumers can filter, but holdings_report_rows filters to ACTIVE itself and does not expose it. That view merges rows sharing (wallet_id, kind, ticker, type_label, name), and two such holdings can differ in status — adding status to the GROUP BY would split the very rows the view exists to merge, while aggregating it would invent a status neither row has.
